source.excerpt: I want to achieve it through not dying.
trail: The checked quotation record gives On Being Funny (1975), page 235, for the version using “it” in the second clause. John Dart also prints that form in a 1977 article; Wikiquote gives a variant repeating “immortality.” These establish transmission, not a claim to have read Lax’s original page. Citation to Eric Lax ↗
The article quotes the same two-sentence joke and credits Allen. John Dart’s 1977 article ↗

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The joke rejects the conventional consolation of surviving through one’s artistic work. A 1970s interview source is cited for this version, while a contemporary discussion of Allen’s writing also records it; the original interview page was not inspected here.
